Synopsis

The npnjs.com phishing campaign hijacked maintainer access for the popular is package. Attackers used social engineering to regain npm access and ship Scavenger malware through trusted releases.

Story

The `is` package compromise followed the npnjs.com phishing pattern. Attackers used social engineering against npm maintainer access, then published malicious versions of a real package with about 2.8 million weekly downloads.

Socket described `is@5.0.0` as different from the Windows-only Scavenger DLL path seen in related packages. This payload was pure JavaScript and cross-platform, running under Node.js on macOS, Linux, and Windows.

The loader reconstructed its payload in memory with a custom decoder and executed it through `new Function`. It collected host, OS, CPU, and environment data, then opened a WebSocket channel. Messages from the socket were treated as executable JavaScript, making the install a live remote shell.

The package is grouped with the broader npm phishing campaign because the method, timing, and maintainer-compromise infrastructure overlap. It remains a distinct record because `is` carried a separate cross-platform JavaScript loader rather than only the Windows DLL family.
